entries.label: ex:catalogue-round-sphere
entries.title: Round shrinking spheres
entries.caption: The normalized sphere in R3 has radius 2. This is the n=2 member of the family.
entries.alt: Round shrinking spheres. The normalized sphere in R3 has radius 2. This is the n=2 member of the family.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-round-cylinder
entries.title: Generalized shrinking cylinders
entries.caption: The R3 cylinder has radius sqrt(2). Only a finite axial window is displayed; there are no end caps.
entries.alt: Generalized shrinking cylinders. The R3 cylinder has radius sqrt(2). Only a finite axial window is displayed; there are no end caps.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-plane-shrinker
entries.title: Planes through the shrinker center
entries.caption: A finite viewing patch of a plane through the origin. Its visible boundary is not part of the complete solution.
entries.alt: Planes through the shrinker center. A finite viewing patch of a plane through the origin. Its visible boundary is not part of the complete solution.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-abresch-langer
entries.title: Abresch--Langer closed shrinking curves
entries.caption: Choose m (turning number) and ℓ (curvature periods) to compute a numerical Abresch–Langer curve. The support function solves h″+h=2/h with period 2πm/ℓ. The fixed drawing and print version show (2, 3). Numerical closing gaps are diagnostics, not certified error bounds.
entries.alt: Numerical Abresch–Langer closed planar curve, initially with turning number 2 and three curvature periods. Controls allow other admissible coprime indices.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-angenent-torus
entries.title: Angenent's shrinking torus
entries.caption: A closed rotational shrinking profile in R3, with outer radius approximately 3.31470827 and inner radius 0.43712397. Return position and angle residuals before mesh rounding are below 1e-9. Numerical closure does not prove existence or uniqueness.
entries.alt: Angenent's shrinking torus. A closed rotational shrinking profile in R3, with outer radius approximately 3.31470827 and inner radius 0.43712397. Return position and angle residuals before mesh rounding are below 1e-9. Numerical closure does not prove existence or uniqueness.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-drugan-sphere
entries.title: Drugan's immersed shrinking spheres
entries.caption: Numerical shooting from pole height b ≈ 0.39345656, reflected at radius ≈ 0.83684239, in R3 with Hvec = −Xperp/2. Blue and orange distinguish the two reflected halves. Use Meridian to see the crossings or change the revolution angle to reveal interior sheets. Cut edges are display boundaries. Numerical diagnostics are not certified error bounds or a uniqueness proof.
entries.alt: Numerically integrated Drugan immersed shrinking sphere. A meridian with self-intersections is revolved about the z-axis; a 270-degree cutaway exposes the sheets.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-clifford-torus
entries.title: The Clifford shrinking torus in four-space
entries.status: Exact R4 geometry, projected to R3
entries.caption: A linear projection of the Clifford torus. The 4D rotation control changes the projection by rotating the second and fourth coordinates. Projected overlaps are not self-intersections of the embedded torus in R4.
entries.alt: The Clifford shrinking torus in four-space. A linear projection of the Clifford torus. The 4D rotation control changes the projection by rotating the second and fourth coordinates. Projected overlaps are not self-intersections of the embedded torus in R4.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-curve-products
entries.title: Products of closed shrinking curves
entries.caption: The product lives in R^(2m). The nonround curve is a numerical Abresch–Langer profile; the product construction is exact once its factors are fixed.
entries.alt: Products of closed shrinking curves. The product lives in R^(2m). The nonround curve is a numerical Abresch–Langer profile; the product construction is exact once its factors are fixed.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-spherical-minimal
entries.title: Higher-codimension spherical shrinkers
entries.caption: The spherical product formula is exact. This shows its factors and ambient dimensions rather than an embedding of a higher-dimensional product in R3.
entries.alt: Higher-codimension spherical shrinkers. The spherical product formula is exact. This shows its factors and ambient dimensions rather than an embedding of a higher-dimensional product in R3.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-moller-genus
entries.title: Møller closed shrinkers of large even genus
entries.caption: Sphere of radius 2 (gold) and non-circular shrinking torus (blue, numerical ODE), following Møller’s Figures 1–2. Dashed red circles mark the intersections and are drawn through the surfaces. Rotate, zoom, toggle the sheets or cutaway, and inspect the meridian. This is the singular input before handle insertion, not a computed finite-genus shrinker.
entries.alt: Møller sphere–torus gluing input: a shaded limiting configuration and meridian show the radius-two sphere, numerical shrinking torus, and two intersection circles. No desingularized surface is computed.

supplementary.caption: Select genus 8, 16, or 24 to see handles replacing both intersection circles. Each displayed mesh is connected, closed, orientable, and has the indicated genus. These are illustrative smoothings of the sphere–torus configuration, not numerical solutions of the self-shrinker equation. The theorem gives no explicit threshold that certifies these particular genera.
supplementary.alt: A genus-eight sphere–torus gluing schematic with two rings of handles; the interactive selector also offers genus sixteen and twenty-four. These are not computed self-shrinkers.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-grim-reaper
entries.title: The grim reaper and its cylinders
entries.caption: Exact formula on a truncated strip. Infinite vertical ends are clipped for display.
entries.alt: The grim reaper and its cylinders. Exact formula on a truncated strip. Infinite vertical ends are clipped for display.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-tilted-grim-reaper
entries.title: Tilted grim-reaper cylinders
entries.caption: Exact tilted grim-reaper formula, with the infinite ends clipped. The displayed tilt parameter is a = 0.65.
entries.alt: Tilted grim-reaper cylinders. Exact tilted grim-reaper formula, with the infinite ends clipped.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-bowl-translator
entries.title: The rotational bowl translator
entries.caption: Numerical integration of the bowl ODE, revolved about its axis; not an exact paraboloid.
entries.alt: The rotational bowl translator. Numerical integration of the bowl ODE, revolved about its axis; not an exact paraboloid.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-translating-catenoid
entries.title: Rotational translating catenoids
entries.caption: Numerical meridian ODE revolved about the translation axis. Both infinite ends are truncated. The displayed neck radius is 1.
entries.alt: Rotational translating catenoids. Numerical meridian ODE revolved about the translation axis. Both infinite ends are truncated.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-delta-wing
entries.title: Strictly convex delta-wing translators
entries.caption: A computed compact patch of the Δ-wing of strip width √2 π, following the paper’s rectangular Dirichlet construction and reflected to translate upward. Rotate the surface, trim its height, or compare longitudinal and transverse profiles with the exact tilted grim-reaper limit. All rim edges are display cuts; this finite-domain approximation has no certified error bound.
entries.alt: A smooth, elongated convex Δ-wing with a rounded minimum and two rising arms. Numerical PDE approximation at strip width square root of two times pi; interactive surface and recentered profile views.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-wang-entire-translators
entries.title: Nonrotational entire convex translators
entries.status: Level-surface schematic and exact limit model
entries.caption: The n = 3 case is a hypersurface in ℝ⁴. Teal shows an illustrative compact level surface in the base ℝ³; switch to a graph slice or increase the rescaling to see the caps leave a fixed spatial window. Ochre shows the exact cylinder {Q = 1} for the k = 2 quadratic blow-down model. The finite shape is not a computed translator, and k = 2 is not asserted for every member. See “How to read this picture” for the drawing formula.
entries.alt: A closed elongated convex level surface with circle symmetry, a two-coordinate graph slice, and the round cylindrical level of a quadratic blow-down. Finite-scale shapes are schematic; the full translator lies in R4.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-prescribed-apex-translators
entries.title: Translators with prescribed apex curvatures
entries.caption: Three surface representatives in ℝ³: the grim-reaper cylinder (0, 1), a numerical Δ-wing with apex Hessian approximately (0.2443, 0.7557), and the rotational bowl (½, ½). Rotate, cut away, and compare principal sections. The Δ-wing uses a finite-domain PDE solve; the bowl uses its ODE. Dashed quadratics in the section view show local data only. Higher-dimensional members are not pictured; all surfaces are truncated and numerical errors are not certified.
entries.alt: Grim-reaper cylinder, anisotropic Delta-wing, and round bowl with their apex curvature pairs and two principal sections.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-scherkenoids
entries.title: Scherkenoid translators
entries.caption: A central sheet opens into alternating grim-reaper-shaped wings. Rotate the model, isolate its fundamental half-strip piece, or change the width w ≥ π to see the wings tilt. The angle is fixed at α = π/2. Based on Hoffman–Martín–White, Figures 5 and 11; upward translation convention. The joining shape is schematic, not an exact or numerically solved Scherkenoid. Outer edges are display cuts.
entries.alt: One connected Scherkenoid schematic with a central sheet and alternating wings joined along vertical reflection lines. Upward convention, alpha pi over two, adjustable strip width at least pi. Not a solved translator.

supplementary.caption: The half-strip for α = π/2, with the boundary heights reflected to the upward convention. The two corners lift to vertical lines on the surface; half-turns about these lines continue the fundamental graph. This diagram shows the domain and boundary data, not an explicit formula for the graph.
supplementary.alt: Half-strip x greater than zero, y between zero and w, with positive infinite height on the horizontal rays and negative infinite height on the finite vertical edge. The corner points mark vertical reflection lines.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-pitchfork
entries.title: The pitchfork translator
entries.caption: The half-width w = π case, in the upward convention. Two graphical halves join along the vertical z-axis; the second is obtained by a half-turn. Rotate the surface, isolate one half, or move through horizontal sections. Based on Hoffman–Martín–White, Figures 6 and 14 and Theorem 12.1. This original drawing is not a numerical solution of the translator equation; all outer edges are display cuts.
entries.alt: A connected pitchfork surface: teal and ochre graphical halves joined along a vertical line, approaching one plane below and three parallel planes above. Original schematic, not a solved translator.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-nguyen-tridents
entries.title: Nguyen translating tridents
entries.caption: One connected Scherk-based drawing with periodic saddle connections, grim-reaper wings, and a central sheet. Rotate, inspect a half surface, or inspect an end view. The displayed neck scales are illustrative; the drawing does not solve the translator equation. All outer edges are display cuts.
entries.alt: Connected trident construction schematic with a row of saddle connections. Two grim-reaper wings rise beside a central sheet; the strip repeats periodically.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-finite-genus-translators
entries.title: Finite-genus translators with three ends
entries.caption: Three upward ends joined through a Scherk-like tunnel belt, following Dávila–del Pino–Nguyen, Theorem 1.1 and Section 2. Rotate, zoom, inspect the cutaway or tunnel detail, and compare the numerical bowl–catenoid input. The connected model is illustrative; it has not been corrected to solve the translator equation. The displayed period counts do not assert existence at those genera.
entries.alt: Connected three-ended construction schematic: a blue bowl sheet and two green catenoid sheets joined through a gold tunnel belt, with a cutaway and enlarged tunnel detail. Not a solved translator.

supplementary.caption: Meridians integrated from the unit-speed rotational translator equations (2.1) and (2.3). The bowl meets the lower wing of the translating catenoid at radius 1.4; revolving this point gives the circle to be desingularized. The height cutoff is artificial.
supplementary.alt: Equal-scale meridian diagram of a numerical bowl and two-wing translating catenoid with one crossing and three upward ends.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-expanding-corners
entries.title: Expanding smoothings of planar corners
entries.caption: The even time-one profile has tip height 1 and is integrated over |x| <= 6. Its asymptotic cone slope is determined by the ODE, not prescribed independently.
entries.alt: Expanding smoothings of planar corners. The even time-one profile has tip height 1 and is integrated over |x| <= 6. Its asymptotic cone slope is determined by the ODE, not prescribed independently.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-rotational-expanders
entries.title: Rotational graphical expanders over round cones
entries.caption: The R3 time-one profile has tip height 1 and is displayed up to radius 6. Its asymptotic cone is determined by this initial value.
entries.alt: Rotational graphical expanders over round cones. The R3 time-one profile has tip height 1 and is displayed up to radius 6. Its asymptotic cone is determined by this initial value.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-two-sheet-expanders
entries.title: Two-sheeted expanders of rotational double cones
entries.caption: Two reflected rotational graphical sheets with tip heights +1 and -1. The sheets share a double cone at infinity and are truncated at radius 6.
entries.alt: Two-sheeted expanders of rotational double cones. Two reflected rotational graphical sheets with tip heights +1 and -1. The sheets share a double cone at infinity and are truncated at radius 6.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-one-sheet-expanders
entries.title: One-sheeted expanders of rotational double cones
entries.caption: Connected rotational expander with neck radius 0.8, shown in the axial window [-5,5]. The drawing makes no claim about a numerically estimated critical cone angle.
entries.alt: One-sheeted expanders of rotational double cones. Connected rotational expander with neck radius 0.8, shown in the axial window [-5,5]. The drawing makes no claim about a numerically estimated critical cone angle.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-mean-convex-expanders
entries.title: One-sided expanders from mean-convex cones
entries.caption: The cone, chosen side, and homothetic leaves illustrate the theorem. No explicit general-cone expander has been computed.
entries.alt: One-sided expanders from mean-convex cones. The cone, chosen side, and homothetic leaves illustrate the theorem. No explicit general-cone expander has been computed.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-expanding-networks
entries.title: Self-expanding planar tree networks
entries.caption: Two numerical four-ended expanders approach the same diagonal rays. Each has two 120-degree triple junctions and a straight central edge. The time control applies Σₜ = √t Σ₁; t = 0 shows only the initial cone. The trees differ with the ends held fixed, but are related by a quarter-turn. Ends are truncated for display.
entries.alt: Two planar expanding trees with the same four diagonal asymptotic rays: a blue horizontal connection and an orange vertical connection, each with two 120-degree junctions.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-stationary-catenoid
entries.title: The catenoid as an eternal stationary flow
entries.caption: The waist radius is 1 and the finite parameter window is |s| <= 1.65. The complete stationary catenoid has two infinite ends.
entries.alt: The catenoid as an eternal stationary flow. The waist radius is 1 and the finite parameter window is |s| <= 1.65. The complete stationary catenoid has two infinite ends.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-whitney-sphere
entries.title: Mean curvature evolution of the Whitney sphere
entries.status: Numerical PDE evolution from exact initial data
entries.caption: Whitney two-sphere in C² (n = 2), with trace mean-curvature speed and the initial scale in the formula above. Four snapshots share a fixed spatial scale. Each pairs a linear R⁴-to-R³ projection with the planar generating profile. Play or select computed times 0 ≤ t ≤ 0.09; this window ends before the singularity and does not specify its time T. Only t = 0 is exact. Additional overlaps may be projection artifacts.
entries.alt: Whitney sphere flow at t = 0, 0.03, 0.06 and 0.09. Surface projections and figure-eight profiles contract and flatten on a common spatial scale; positive-time geometry is numerical.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-degenerate-neckpinches
entries.title: Rotational degenerate neckpinch solutions
entries.status: Asymptotic time sequence with numerical bowl cap
entries.caption: Three illustrative times approach the odd-cubic degenerate neckpinch; the fourth panel is a singular cusp target. All four use the same spatial scale. Rotate, play toward the singular time, compare meridians, or inspect the cylinder, intermediate profile, and bowl limits. Compact slices and joins are schematic, not a numerical MCF evolution; only the limiting bowl is integrated from its ODE. Shown in R3 with n=2, m=3, K=1.
entries.alt: Four views at a common spatial scale show the left tip advancing toward the origin and sharpening into a one-sided cusp. The outer cap persists. The compact surfaces are asymptotic schematics with numerical bowl caps.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-angenent-oval
entries.title: The Angenent oval as an explicit ancient flow
entries.caption: The planar ancient oval satisfies cos(x)=exp(t) cosh(y). The time slider shows finite negative times; its smooth flow exists for all t<0. The time slider uses a fixed spatial scale.
entries.alt: The Angenent oval as an explicit ancient flow. The planar ancient oval satisfies cos(x)=exp(t) cosh(y). The time slider shows finite negative times; its smooth flow exists for all t<0.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-kkm-one-end
entries.title: Kapouleas–Kleene–Møller shrinkers with one end
entries.caption: A connected model joins two sphere-like caps, an inner disk, and one outer sheet through a periodic Scherk belt. Rotate or use Cutaway to inspect the joining region. The period count and conical waviness are illustrative; this is not a numerically solved KKM shrinker. The theorem applies only to sufficiently large genus, with no explicit threshold. The outer edge is a display truncation.
entries.alt: Connected Scherk-based sphere–plane construction model with a ring of saddle-shaped openings, spherical caps, an inner disk and one wavy outer sheet. Not a computed self-shrinker.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-drugan-nguyen-torus
entries.title: Drugan–Nguyen variational shrinking tori
entries.caption: Weighted half-plane construction of a closed geodesic; no identity with the numerical Angenent profile is assumed.
entries.alt: Weighted half-plane construction of a closed geodesic; no identity with the numerical Angenent profile is assumed.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-bns-genus
entries.title: Buzano–Nguyen–Schulz shrinkers of every positive genus
entries.caption: Informed by Buzano–Nguyen–Schulz, Section 4, Figures 3–4; not a numerical solution of the shrinker equation. Choose a genus or use Cutaway to see the interior. Outer rims and cut edges are display boundaries.
entries.alt: Genus-three schematic: a rounded cap with alternating openings joins a central sheet to one noncompact outer sheet; a vertical cutaway exposes the interior. Not a computed shrinker.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-ketover-doubled-plane
entries.title: Ketover self-shrinking doubled planes
entries.caption: Informed by Ketover, Proposition 7.4 and Section 8: two sheets joined by g + 1 necks near a circle. Rotate, choose a genus, or use Cutaway to inspect the connections. Two ends are proved only for sufficiently large genus; the displayed choices do not specify a threshold. This is not a computed shrinker.
entries.alt: Genus-five schematic with six smooth necks joining upper and lower sheets around a circle. Each sheet extends outward toward a conical end. A cutaway exposes the neck walls. Both outer rims are display truncations, not boundaries of the complete surface.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-spherical-doubling-shrinkers
entries.title: Closed shrinkers from spherical doubling
entries.caption: Two nearby spherical sheets are joined through 2m radial necks on two aligned latitude circles. Rotate, zoom, or use Cutaway to see the inner sheet. The sites follow a numerically computed balanced linearized latitude guide; neck sizes and sheet separation are enlarged drawing choices. The m = 6, 10, 14 models illustrate genus 2m − 1 and are not asserted to lie in the theorem’s sufficiently-large-m range. This is not a solved self-shrinker or a certified approximation.
entries.alt: A connected closed surface with blue outer and gold inner spherical sheets joined through copper-colored radial necks on two aligned latitude circles. A cutaway exposes the inner sheet; the standalone drawing also shows a local neck section. Construction schematic, not a numerical self-shrinker.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-sun-wang-torus-translators
entries.title: Translators with an Angenent-torus end
entries.status: Numerical Angenent profile; auxiliary end model
entries.caption: Sun–Wang, Theorem 1.2 and Appendix A: the leading model (√z x, z), x ∈ S_A, with the unknown normal correction set to u = 0. The rotational quotient shows one connected end; the horizontal slice restores the rotation angle to show a torus in ℝ³. Use the height slider to see √z growth, or divide x by √z to see the cylindrical rescaling. The Angenent profile is numerically integrated, not a circular torus. Here h = z/z₀ with an unspecified sufficiently large cutoff z₀; h = 1 is not a tip. The compact core, correction, and fattening pair are not computed. This is not a solved translator.
entries.alt: A widening tube in the rotational quotient of the auxiliary end in four-space, and a numerical Angenent torus at the selected height. Copper marks the selected horizontal section. The quotient suppresses the rotation angle; its open rims are display truncations.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-sun-wang-sphere-doubling-translators
entries.title: Translators with high-genus spherical-doubling ends
entries.caption: Sun–Wang, equations (3.1)–(3.2): horizontal slices grow like √z times the prescribed shrinker. Rotate the connected spherical-doubling model, expose its necks with Cutaway, or vary height and rescale by 1/√z. These are two-dimensional slices of one three-dimensional end in ℝ⁴. The input shrinker is schematic; the unknown normal correction and compact core are omitted. Displayed bridge counts are illustrative, not existence thresholds.
entries.alt: A cutaway horizontal slice exposes gold inner and blue outer spherical sheets joined by twenty copper necks on two aligned latitude circles. Its model genus is nineteen. Height controls square-root growth; rescaling removes this growth. Schematic slices of one end in four-space, not a computed translator.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-ancient-torus-curves
entries.title: Ancient torus curves in higher codimension
entries.status: Exact R4 curve, projected to R3
entries.caption: Frequencies (1,2). The time slider numerically inverts r²+r⁸=−2t in the exact formula; the viewing scale stays fixed. Apparent crossings may result from projection.
entries.alt: Frequencies (1,2). The time slider numerically inverts r²+r⁸=−2t in the exact formula; the viewing scale stays fixed. Apparent crossings may result from projection.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-eternal-helices
entries.title: Eternal shrinking helices
entries.caption: The time slider inverts log r+r²/2=1/2−t. Only −5π/2 ≤ s ≤ 5π/2 is drawn; both infinite ends are omitted. The viewing scale stays fixed.
entries.alt: The time slider inverts log r+r²/2=1/2−t. Only −5π/2 ≤ s ≤ 5π/2 is drawn; both infinite ends are omitted. The viewing scale stays fixed.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-double-plane-flow
entries.title: Immortal annuli converging to a double plane
entries.caption: Rotate the annulus, use the cutaway, and compare earlier, intermediate, and later finite stages with the separate limit t → ∞. The viewing scale is fixed. The compressed radial profile shows the fixed asymptotic heights ±h. Shapes and stage spacing are illustrative, not computed PDE time slices or a convergence rate.
entries.alt: Three schematic finite-time annuli with decreasing positive neck radii and locally flattening sheets, followed by one limiting plane counted twice. Far ends retain their asymptotic planes.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-double-sphere-flow
entries.title: Immortal compact flows converging to a double sphere
entries.caption: Three ordered finite-time stages and the infinite-time double-sphere limit. Blue and ochre sheets join through two polar necks; the profiles below show their approach to y = 0. For n = 2 the radial drawing (p, y) ↦ (1 + 2y)p displays the product coordinate as radial separation and distorts the metric. Cutaway edges are display cuts, not surface boundaries. These are schematic stages, not computed PDE slices; no physical times or decay rates are assigned.
entries.alt: Three finite-time cutaway tori with two progressively smaller polar necks and closer blue and ochre sheets, followed by one sphere marked multiplicity two. Matching closed orbit-space profiles flatten to a doubled segment. Schematic radial coordinate drawings of a flow in S² × R, not Euclidean MCF.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-nguyen-shrinking-saddles
entries.title: Nguyen's one-ended shrinking saddles
entries.caption: A connected sphere–plane construction model with two caps, an inner disk, and one outer sheet joined through a Scherk saddle belt. Rotate it, open the cutaway, or inspect the unwrapped Scherk minimal surface. The displayed period counts illustrate genus m − 1; the existence theorem requires sufficiently large m. The global shape and conical profile are schematic, not a solved shrinker.
entries.alt: Connected Nguyen construction schematic with a periodic saddle belt, a cutaway exposing the inner disk and lower cap, and an unwrapped Scherk ingredient. Not a computed self-shrinker.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-angenent-torus-cylinders
entries.title: Angenent torus cylinders
entries.caption: Three slices w = −12, 0, 12 of the numerical Angenent torus × R in R4, projected into R3. Use 4D rotation to change the projection. These are selected slices of one connected three-dimensional hypersurface, not three components or its entire geometry.
entries.alt: Three selected slices of the torus-cylinder in R4, with fourth-coordinate rotation before projection.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-iw-two-ended
entries.title: Ilmanen–White two-ended shrinkers
entries.caption: An upper graph and its reflection join along h + 1 equatorial neck curves and flare into two conical ends. The default genus h = 3 follows the topology of Figure 1 in Ilmanen–White (the paper uses g = h + 1). Rotate, select a genus, or use Cutaway and Equator z = 0 to inspect the necks. This is an original schematic, not Chopp’s numerical surface or a solution of the shrinker equation. Neck shapes, scale and cone slopes are illustrative; both outer rims truncate infinite ends.
entries.alt: Genus-three Ilmanen–White schematic: two reflected curved sheets joined by four smooth necks, with two flaring ends. A second cutaway view exposes the neck walls. Not a computed self-shrinker.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-shao-zou-stacking
entries.title: Shao–Zou shrinkers with any prescribed number of ends
entries.caption: Connected sheets with open catenoidal necks: each consecutive pair is joined at m sites, and consecutive gaps are staggered by π/m. The default k = 4, m = 10 model has 30 bridges, four truncated ends and genus 27. Rotate, zoom, use the cutaway, or change k and m; Neck layout shows the alternating site sets. Radial profiles are guided by the paper’s linearized solutions, with enlarged separation and neck widths. Finite-m balancing, tilts, Gaussian-metric neck corrections and the nonlinear shrinker equation are not solved; end slopes are illustrative. Existence requires sufficiently large m for each fixed k. Open drawing shows the fixed four-sheet reference.
entries.alt: Shao–Zou construction schematic: four colored sheets joined through thirty staggered open necks, with four truncated ends; a cutaway exposes the connections and a plan diagram shows alternating neck sites.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-hmw-platonic-polygon
entries.title: Flow-generated Platonic and polygonal shrinkers
entries.caption: A rounded cubical shell with six radial passages illustrates genus five and avoidance of the six face-center rays. Select any Platonic symmetry or a regular polygon, show the excluded rays Q, and use Cutaway to reveal the inner wall. Inspired by Section 4 and Theorem 24 of Hoffman–Martín–White; the cubical silhouette also recalls Chopp’s numerical picture in Figure 2. These original compact models illustrate the topology of the construction input. They are not computed self-shrinkers or simulated flow slices, and do not establish compactness of the tangent shrinkers. The sufficiently large polygonal shrinkers are noncompact.
entries.alt: A rounded cubical surface with six openings and genus five, a cutaway exposing its central cavity, and a sevenfold polygonal construction model. Schematics, not computed shrinkers.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-hmw-one-ended
entries.title: Flow-generated sphere–plane shrinkers
entries.caption: An original connected genus-g model informed by Hoffman–Martín–White, Figures 1, 5–6 and Theorems 40–42. Rotate the surface, remove its front half, inspect the g+1 horizontal lines, or compare with the separate sphere–plane limit. The model has one exterior sheet; exactly one end is proved only for sufficiently large genus. Shape and cone slope are illustrative, not a computed self-shrinker. Gold and blue distinguish its two sides; outer and cut edges are display boundaries.
entries.alt: Hoffman–Martín–White sphere–plane topology schematic: alternating openings join rounded caps to a central sheet and exterior. Full surface and cutaway, with a separate radius-two sphere and plane limit. Not a computed shrinker.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-hmw-three-ended
entries.title: Flow-generated three-ended shrinkers
entries.caption: An original connected topology model informed by Hoffman–Martín–White, Figure 7 and Theorem 43. Three exterior sheets are joined by alternating open necks. Rotate, zoom, use the cutaway, inspect the neck layout, or compare with the separate multiplicity-three plane limit. The model has genus 2g; three-ended existence is proved only for sufficiently large g. The paper’s genus-two picture is conjectural. Neck sizes, end slopes and separation are illustrative; no shrinker equation has been solved. Outer rims and cut edges are display boundaries.
entries.alt: Connected three-ended HMW topology schematic with alternating upper and lower necks. Full view, cutaway and neck plan; model g = 3, genus six. Not a computed shrinker.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-ketover-platonic
entries.title: Ketover shrinkers with Platonic symmetry
entries.caption: Two spherical sheets are joined by one radial neck at each face center, following Ketover’s doubling sweepout (pp. 2 and 9–10). Choose a Platonic solid to see 4, 6, 8, 12, or 20 necks and genus 3, 5, 7, 11, or 19. Cutaway reveals the inner sheet; display separation enlarges the gap. Colors mark parts of one connected surface. These are compact comparison surfaces with illustrative neck sizes, not computed self-shrinkers. Compactness and ends of the min-max limits remain undetermined.
entries.alt: Full and cutaway views of two spherical sheets joined through six face-center necks in the cube arrangement, giving genus five. Five models show all Platonic face-center arrangements. Original construction schematic, not a solved self-shrinker.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-swz-large-entropy
entries.title: Sun–Wang–Zhou shrinkers of arbitrarily large entropy
entries.caption: A qualitative increasing curve illustrates the growth of Gaussian widths with the min-max parameter k. For dimensions two through six the constructed shrinker has entropy equal to the kth width, with growth comparable to k to the power one over n plus one and Gaussian Morse index at most k. No numerical entropy values or shapes are plotted.
entries.alt: A qualitative increasing curve illustrates the growth of Gaussian widths with the min-max parameter k. For dimensions two through six the constructed shrinker has entropy equal to the kth width, with growth comparable to k to the power one over n plus one and Gaussian Morse index at most k. No numerical entropy values or shapes are plotted.

entries.title: Chu–Sun genus-one shrinkers below the shrinking doughnut
entries.caption: A generic torus icon represents the topology of the starting Drugan–Nguyen rotational shrinker T. An ancient mean curvature flow and a singular blow-up produce a genus-one shrinker Sigma of strictly lower entropy. The final box deliberately leaves compactness, ends, symmetry, and geometric shape unspecified.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-scherk-translators
entries.title: Doubly periodic Scherk translators
entries.status: Numerical PDE approximation with illustrative corner fills
entries.caption: The rectangular case α = w = π/2, computed with finite edge heights ±2.5 and reflected to the upward convention. The orange fundamental patch extends by half-turns about its vertical corner lines; blue copies show the periodic arrangement. Rotate, zoom, isolate the patch, or crop the height. Small unresolved corner regions are filled for display. This is an uncertified approximation, not a closed formula; all outer edges are truncations.
entries.alt: Numerical Scherk translator: an orange saddle patch connects to blue half-turn copies on a checkerboard lattice. Upward translation. Finite boundary data and small illustrative corner fills; no certified error bound.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-translating-helicoids
entries.title: Helicoid-like translators
entries.caption: Tilted alignment of vertical reflection lines and alternating strip patches. Only a finite viewing window is shown; the mesh is heuristic and does not solve the translator equation.
entries.alt: Helicoid-like translators. Tilted alignment of vertical reflection lines and alternating strip patches. Only a finite viewing window is shown; the mesh is heuristic and does not solve the translator equation.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-translating-annuloids
entries.title: Annuloid translators in slabs
entries.caption: Heuristic capped annuloid: two strip-like sheets joined around a neck. The shape is not computed from the translator PDE, and no pictured neck size specifies the paper’s parameters.
entries.alt: Annuloid translators in slabs. Heuristic capped annuloid: two strip-like sheets joined around a neck. The shape is not computed from the translator PDE, and no pictured neck size specifies the paper’s parameters.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-mountain-pass-expanders
entries.title: Mountain-pass self-expanders
entries.caption: An ordering diagram for two strictly stable barriers and an intervening expander. The curves are symbolic slices; they do not prescribe topology or demonstrate a solution.
entries.alt: Mountain-pass self-expanders. An ordering diagram for two strictly stable barriers and an intervening expander. The curves are symbolic slices; they do not prescribe topology or demonstrate a solution.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-high-genus-expanders
entries.title: Expanders of unbounded genus at a fixed cone
entries.caption: One connected model with three conical ends. Rotate, cut away the front, compare reflection-slice types, or change the model genus while keeping the same illustrative cone. The paper obtains four classes (small/big, type 1/type 2) by degree theory; the mesh does not distinguish small from big. No expander PDE is solved. The displayed k = 4 and cone opening are drawing choices, not verified existence parameters. Open the drawing for the slice-pairing diagrams.
entries.alt: Connected three-ended topology model and cutaway, with type 1 and type 2 reflection-slice diagrams. Not a computed self-expander.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-knotted-expanders
entries.title: Knotted self-expanders
entries.caption: A trefoil tube with three attached annular ends, following Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 3.2. Rotate to inspect the crossings; switch views to see the closed tube and three punctures. The colored ends flare only to suggest conical asymptotics. This mesh is not a computed expander.
entries.alt: A connected two-dimensional trefoil tube with three open colored ends. The crossings pass above and below one another. Genus one; three display rims. Topology schematic, not a numerical self-expander.

supplementary.caption: Thicken the trefoil, remove three disks, and attach three annuli. The genus stays one. In the paper, expanding annular barriers protect the overpass bridges during minimization (Figure 2). The drawings illustrate the topology, not the geometric Plateau solutions.
supplementary.alt: Three stages: a closed trefoil tube, the tube with three punctures, and the tube continued into three annular ends.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-hh-ancient-ovals
entries.title: Haslhofer--Hershkovits ancient ovals
entries.caption: Surface case n = 2, j = 1: numerical rotational mean curvature flow from a long convex seed, following the limiting-construction strategy. Compare times, play the evolution, rotate, or inspect the meridian and the tip. The default view divides lengths by √(−t); Original size keeps the physical spatial scale fixed. Extinction is normalized to t = 0 and length/width = 2 at t = −1. These finite-seed computations are not certified slices of the ancient solution.
entries.alt: Four time slices of a numerical convex surface flow in three-space, from an elongated oval to an almost round sphere. Each is divided by square root of minus time at a common scale. Interactive time, rotation, zoom, meridian and bowl-tip comparisons.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-minimal-ancient-flows
entries.title: Ancient flows from unstable minimal hypersurfaces
entries.status: Numerical Costa surface and linearized time model
entries.caption: Four model times on the positive normal side of the Costa surface; switch sides, play, rotate, or inspect the stationary limit. The sampled surface has one handle and three truncated ends. Time follows a positive numerical Dirichlet Jacobi mode on the truncated surface, not the nonlinear ancient flow of Mramor–Payne. Normal displacements are magnified ×3 by default; ×1 restores model scale. The same camera and spatial scale are used for every panel.
entries.alt: Four views of a genus-one Costa surface with three open ends, moving away from the stationary minimal surface along a positive linearized mode. The opposite side is selectable. These are numerical linearized model views, not computed nonlinear ancient slices.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-reapernoid
entries.title: The eternal reapernoid
entries.caption: Four numerical slices in ℝ³ move outward from a unit-neck catenoid, at one spatial scale. Play or drag the time slider, rotate, zoom, or switch to meridians in ℝ³ and ℝ⁴. The three-space meridian flattens after recentering; the four-space meridian approaches a grim reaper. These are finite-start, truncated-domain PDE approximations of the construction, not exact formulas or a certified eternal limit. Open rims cut the displayed surface at x = ±2.
entries.alt: Four numerical reapernoid surfaces in three-space at times −8, −4, 0 and 10. The annular neck grows outward, with radii approximately 1.034, 1.251, 2 and 5.327. All surfaces use the same camera and spatial scale.

supplementary.status: Numerical profiles and proved forward limits
supplementary.caption: Profiles are translated by subtracting the current neck radius, without rescaling. Blue curves show computed finite times; gold dashed curves show the limits in Theorem 1.3. The ℝ³ limit is a line. The ℝ⁴ case represents the higher-dimensional grim-reaper behavior and is shown only as a meridian. Neither limit is asserted at a finite time.
supplementary.alt: Recentered numerical meridians at four times. The three-space profiles flatten toward a horizontal line, while the four-space profiles approach a grim reaper. The higher-dimensional picture is a profile, not a surface in three-space.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-stacked-pancakes
entries.title: Ancient stacked pancakes
entries.caption: Original illustration informed by Mramor–Yudowitz, Theorem 1.1, Figure 1 and Sections 2.2–3.1. A three-dimensional linear section shows two flattened lobes joined by one neck (copper). The actual hypersurface has dimension n ≥ 3 in ℝⁿ⁺¹; the displayed section is not itself a mean curvature flow in ℝ³. Rotate and zoom, close the cutaway with Revolve, or inspect the meridian. The drawn proportions are illustrative; no evolution equation is solved.
entries.alt: Schematic three-dimensional section of two flattened pancakes connected by one central neck, with a quarter removed to expose the connection. The actual ambient dimension is at least four.

supplementary.caption: The right profile r = u(x,t) has exactly two local maxima and one positive local minimum at the neck; the two poles lie on the rotation axis. Reflection across x = 0 exchanges the lobes. The dashed horizontal boundaries mark a fixed containing slab, not the moving caps. Away from the poles, each profile point represents an Sⁿ⁻¹ orbit in the full hypersurface. This qualitative drawing is not to scale and asserts no catenoid asymptotics.
supplementary.alt: Annotated symmetric meridian: two radius maxima, one central neck minimum, two poles on the vertical axis, the reflection plane, and two boundaries of a fixed containing slab.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-ancient-spiral-curves
entries.title: Compact nonconvex ancient spiral curves
entries.caption: Four ancient-regime times on one spatial scale, with animation and a cap close-up. The Yin–Yang arms are computed from the rotating-soliton ODE; the closing cap uses the corrected grim-reaper ansatz of Section 2. Blue arms rotate counterclockwise, while the orange cap moves clockwise and inward. This illustrates the asymptotic construction, not numerically evolved slices of the ancient PDE solution. The displayed interval does not extend to extinction.
entries.alt: Four closed Yin–Yang spiral models at t = −24, −18, −12 and −8, shrinking and losing turns, with the outer closing cap marked orange.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-grim-reaper-chains
entries.title: Eternal curves from chains of grim reapers
entries.caption: Angenent–You, equation (3), §3.1–3.3 and Figure 9. Equal strips aₖ = kπ and shifts Cₖ = 0. Play the evolution or compare six times from t = −6 to 9 at a fixed scale. The model overlay shows exact separate grim reapers, with velocities −1, +1, −1. The blue curve is computed from smoothly joined data at t = −10, with distant truncated ends; it is not a closed formula or a certified approximation of the eternal limit. Zero is an ordinary time, not an extinction time.
entries.alt: Six numerical time slices of one planar curve with three alternating grim-reaper turns, evolving from separated turns to a broader profile. Both outer ends continue to the left along y = 0 and y = 3π. Finite-start numerical approximation.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-mobius-shrinker
entries.title: The Lee–Wang self-shrinking Mobius bundle
entries.caption: A finite patch of the exact embedded Möbius quotient in C². Rotation changes the projection; projected crossings do not imply self-intersection.
entries.alt: A finite patch of the exact embedded Möbius quotient in C². Rotation changes the projection; projected crossings do not imply self-intersection.

entries.label: ex:catalogue-jlt-compact-shrinkers
entries.title: Compact periodic Lagrangian quadric shrinkers
entries.caption: The ODE and rational phase-closing conditions produce a compact immersion with domain Sⁿ⁻¹ × S¹. No numerical closed orbit or embeddedness is claimed by this picture.
entries.alt: The ODE and rational phase-closing conditions produce a compact immersion with domain Sⁿ⁻¹ × S¹. No numerical closed orbit or embeddedness is claimed by this picture.

entries.title: Joyce–Lee–Tsui small-angle Lagrangian translators

entries.alt: The exact integral parametrization in C² with a₁ = a₂ = 1 and α = 1/2, evaluated numerically. Both planar ends are truncated. This is a projection, not an R³ expander.
